summary: The clearest signal in the data is structural: all 8 missed Exhaustion Short events over 30 days were blocked exclusively by the prev_day_rally gate, with actual prior-day move values ranging from -0.48% to +0.63% against a threshold of 6.0% — meaning the gate is not measuring the right precondition. These missed stocks (ADANIENT -9.18%, ADANIPORTS -6.79%, ADANIGREEN -6.88%, GODREJIND -5.14%, PFIZER -5.84%) fell hard without a prior single-day rally, driven instead by sector/conglomerate news shocks — a scenario the current OR logic (prev_day_rally OR cumul_rally OR gap_up) should theoretically catch, but the gap_up and cumul_rally arms also appear to have failed. The best fix is structural: replace the single-day rally precondition with a gap-down-open trigger as an additional OR arm, since all five sample missed stocks opened near or below prior close (no gap up) yet fell sharply intraday, suggesting an intraday high exhaustion pattern rather than a post-rally exhaustion pattern.

proposals.reasoning: Even setting aside the gap-down arm above, the threshold of 6.0% is empirically too high: ADANIENT's actual value of 0.63% is the highest of the 5 sample missed stocks, meaning even halving the threshold to 3.0% would not have caught them via this arm. However, lowering to 3.5% would widen the net for stocks that rallied modestly (2-4%) over the prior day and then exhausted intraday — a genuine sub-pattern not covered by the structural fix above. The cumul_rally and gap_up arms provide the other coverage layers, so loosening this single arm by ~40% does not open the floodgates. The spike-candle gates remain the primary quality filter.
proposals.expected_impact: Marginal increase in signals for stocks with 3.5-6% prior-day rallies. Does not fix the 8 missed signals (all had values below 1%), but prevents over-filtering in the moderate-rally sub-case. Estimated +1-2 signals per month.
proposals.skip_reason: LOW confidence — noted but not auto-applied

proposals.title: Add gap-down open or flat open as a standalone qualifying arm in the rally precondition OR-gate
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant EXH_GAP_DOWN_TRIGGER_PCT = -0.5 and a new boolean arm had_gap_down = (gap_up_pct <= EXH_GAP_DOWN_TRIGGER_PCT). Insert this into the existing OR condition so it reads: if not (had_rally or had_cumul or had_gap_up or had_gap_down). This arm captures stocks that open flat-to-down but then spike intraday on news (conglomerate, sector, macro) and exhaust from a local intraday high rather than a multi-day rally high. It should be placed immediately after the existing gap_up_pct computation, before the `if not (had_rally or had_cumul or had_gap_up)` block. The existing spike-candle gates (c5_move_pct, c5_turnover, same-slot volume, vol_ratio) remain unchanged and will still filter out weak signals that slip through on the new arm.
proposals.reasoning: All 8 missed signals over 30 days were blocked solely by prev_day_rally. Of the 5 sample cases: ADANIENT actual_value=0.63% (threshold 6.0%), ADANIPORTS 0.09%, ADANIGREEN -0.48%, GODREJIND -0.1%, PFIZER -0.4%. None had a prior-day rally, none had a meaningful gap up (gap_up_pct would be near zero or negative given flat/down opens), and the 3-day cumul_rally arm also failed them. Yet all fell 5-9% from their intraday high — textbook intraday exhaustion. The pattern is news-shock intraday spike (not a multi-day rally) followed by profit-booking. The current gate architecture has no arm for this case.
proposals.expected_impact: Recovers up to 8 missed signals over the 30-day window. The spike-candle volume and move gates already in place will reject low-quality entries on this new arm, so false positive rate should remain controlled. Net expected addition: 2-4 genuine signals per month that currently fall through entirely.

proposals.title: Require the intraday spike candle to occur at or above the prior-day high (PDH) as a structural level gate
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant EXH_REQUIRE_SPIKE_AT_PDH = True and a new gate: if EXH_REQUIRE_SPIKE_AT_PDH and c5_close < float(daily['High'].iloc[-2]): _dbg_fail and continue. Place this gate immediately after the existing c5_close > c5_open (green candle) check and before the c5_move_pct check. This ensures that when had_gap_down is the qualifying arm (new arm from proposal 1), the intraday spike must have reached at least the PDH level to qualify as a structural exhaustion — preventing random intraday bounces on down-gap stocks from triggering the panel.
proposals.reasoning: If proposal 1 (gap-down arm) is implemented, there is a risk of catching intraday bounces that are not true exhaustion spikes. The 5 sample missed stocks (ADANIENT day_high 3148.1, ADANIPORTS 1709.1, etc.) all made significant intraday highs. Requiring the spike candle to reach or exceed PDH when the stock opened flat/down adds a structural anchor — the spike must have genuinely reclaimed yesterday's high, which is what trapped the late buyers. This is a tightening gate that specifically governs the new gap-down arm pathway.
proposals.expected_impact: Reduces false positives from the new gap-down arm. Slightly reduces recovered signal count (from ~8 to estimated ~5-6) but improves the quality of those signals. Net: tighter, more reliable signals on news-shock exhaustion days.

proposals.title: Cap the confidence score vol_s component denominator to prevent it from saturating at very low volume thresholds
proposals.proposed_change: In the confidence scoring block, the current vol_s formula is: min(day_vol / (PDH_VOL_MIN * 3), 1.0) * 35. With PDH_VOL_MIN = 500_000, saturation occurs at 1,500,000 shares. Add a new constant PDH_VOL_SCORE_CAP = 3_000_000 and change the formula to: min(day_vol / PDH_VOL_SCORE_CAP, 1.0) * 35. This doubles the volume required to reach max vol_s score from 1.5M to 3M shares, reducing the number of moderate-volume stocks scoring STRONG (>=65) purely on volume. Place this change only in the confidence scoring section, not in the liquidity gate.
proposals.reasoning: The signal outcome statistics are empty ({}), so no direct win-rate data exists for PDH Breakout. However, with PDH_VOL_MIN rolled back to 500,000 (from a higher auto-tuned value per the code comment on 2026-07-13), the vol_s component saturates at just 1.5M shares — a modest volume for Nifty 500 names. This means stocks with 1.5M shares in an early session (well before full liquidity develops) can reach the maximum vol_s contribution of 35 points. Tightening the saturation cap to 3M penalises early, thin signals without changing the admission gate itself.
proposals.expected_impact: Fewer STRONG-labelled signals in the first 60-90 minutes of trade when volume is still building. GOOD-labelled signals increase proportionally. No change in signal count, only in confidence label distribution. Reduces overconfident early entries.

proposals.title: Tighten MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT to filter out wide confirmation candles that indicate absorption failure
proposals.proposed_change: Change MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT from 0.18 to a new constant evaluated as follows: add EXH_GAP_DOWN_TRIGGER_PCT — no, separately add MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT_TIGHT = 0.12 and use that as the gate threshold instead of 0.18. The proposed_change is: set MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT = 0.12. The gate logic (confirm_range_pct >= MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT) remains structurally identical; only the constant value changes. No other code modifications needed.
proposals.reasoning: Signal outcome statistics are empty ({}), preventing direct win-rate citation. However, the concept behind the confirmation candle gate is that a tight next-candle range signals calm absorption. At 0.18% of price, a stock at Rs 500 can have a Rs 0.90 range on the confirmation candle — already a non-trivial intraday swing that is not obviously 'calm'. Tightening to 0.12% (Rs 0.60 on a Rs 500 stock) better matches the intent of the gate: the confirmation candle should be genuinely narrow, not just narrower than a wide candle. This is a conservative tightening that reduces the number of borderline confirmations passing.
proposals.expected_impact: Reduces Momentum Breakout signal count modestly (estimated -15 to -25% of signals that currently pass confirm_range_pct at 0.13-0.18%). Increases average confirmation candle quality. Given no win-rate data, magnitude of quality improvement is uncertain.

proposals.title: Add a minimum zone_age floor to prevent same-week zones from scoring artificially high on freshness
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant DZ_MIN_ZONE_AGE_DAYS = 2 and a gate immediately after the zone_level is found: if zone_age < DZ_MIN_ZONE_AGE_DAYS: _dbg_fail(_debug, 'zone_too_fresh', symbol, zone_age=zone_age, needed_min=DZ_MIN_ZONE_AGE_DAYS) and continue. The rationale is that a base+impulse pair from the prior day (zone_age=1) has not had time for a genuine retest — the price is merely returning to a level that formed yesterday, which is better described as a pullback than a zone retest. Place this gate immediately after the zone_level is None check and before the DZ_PROXIMITY_PCT retest gate.
proposals.reasoning: Signal outcome statistics are empty ({}) for this panel. The current freshness scoring formula fresh_s = max(0.0, (DZ_ZONE_LOOKBACK_DAYS - zone_age) / DZ_ZONE_LOOKBACK_DAYS) * 25 awards the maximum 25 freshness points to zone_age=1 (yesterday's zone). A base+impulse from yesterday that price immediately revisits today is likely still within the impulse's retracement, not a true institutional retest. Filtering zone_age < 2 removes the most structurally ambiguous cases. DZ_ZONE_LOOKBACK_DAYS=15 means a 2-day minimum still allows zones from the past 13 days to qualify, preserving most of the signal universe.
proposals.expected_impact: Reduces signals on days immediately following a base+impulse formation (estimated -10 to -20% of signals). Improves structural clarity of remaining signals. Given no win-rate data, quality improvement magnitude is uncertain but the conceptual case is clear.
